- "smørgås-kampagne" - This is interesting. "Smørgås" is actually Norwegian/Danish for "smørrebrød" (open sandwich). In Danish, the word is "smørrebrød" or "smørgås" is more Norwegian. Actually "smørgås" exists in Norwegian; in Danish it's "smørrebrød". The term "smear campaign" in English - the German original might be "Smear-Kampagne" or "Schmähkampagne". Hmm, that's odd. Actually, in German, "smear campaign" is "Verleumdungskampagne" or "Schmutzkampagne". The word "smear" in English... The article says FIFA accused UEFA of a "smear campaign". If the original English was "smear campaign", a machine translation might have produced "smørekampagne" or "bagvaskelseskampagne". "Smørgås-kampagne" is bizarre - it literally means "sandwich campaign". This is likely a machine translation error where "smear" was confused with "smörgås"/"smorgasbord" (smörgåsbord = "smørrebrødsbord"). Actually "smorgasbord" in Swedish is "smörgåsbord". So "smear" → "smörgås" confusion is plausible in a bad MT. In Danish, the correct term would be "bagvaskelseskampagne" or "smædekampagne" (smear campaign = "smædekampagne" is actually a real Danish term!). "Smæde" means to smear/slander. So "smædekampagne" would be correct Danish. "Smørgås-kampagne" is nonsense Danish - it's a sandwich. Also the hyphenation "smørgås-kampagne" with hyphen is not standard Danish compound writing (Danish writes compounds together: "smørgåskampagne" if it were a word). The title also uses 'smørgås-kampagne'.
